messages:
anya_support: FYI customer ACME reporting massive 5xx and timeouts on /v1/generate since ~09:06 UTC. They see gateway errors and high latency. Correlation IDs: req=acme-req-9f7c. Request example below.

acme_infra: we're seeing 502s and 504s across hosts in us-west-2, started around 09:05. Some of our requests to Redwood show "upstream timed out" in the logs. Can you confirm?

ryan_oncall: thanks @anya_support @acme_infra — I'm looking. I see spikes in error rates and an alert from infra for redis/cache-prd-1 latency > 2s. @kevin_sre can you take a look at cache side?

kevin_sre: joining. From Redis dashboard: >90% CPU, evictions spiked, and a few clients getting 'OOM command not allowed' errors. There's also a sharp increase in blocked clients metric. Looks like prefix/KV cache is thrashing. Logs:
```
[2026-03-15T09:05:42Z] redis-1: accepted 1200 connections, blocked_clients: 47
[2026-03-15T09:06:01Z] redis-1: evicted 82000 keys, used_memory_rss: 48G, used_memory: 46G
[2026-03-15T09:06:18Z] redis-1: MISCONF Redis is configured to save RDB snapshots, but the server is currently not able to persist on disk: RDB child has exited with error
```

deploy-bot: Incident #INC-20260315-17 created (priority: P0) by ryan_oncall. Paging infra/SRE/Support.

anya_support: Customer repro snippet (from them):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-ACME" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-13b","input":"summarize: ...","request_id":"acme-req-9f7c"}' 
```
They get a 502 with body: `{ "error": "upstream service error: cache timeout" }` and sometimes 504.

ryan_oncall: I'm seeing our gateway logs show long tail on calls to prefix-KV service: 95th pct latency ~ 3.8s. Client-side timeouts configured at 3s, so we see gateway aborts -> 502/504. Evidence:
```
[proxy] request_id=acme-req-9f7c upstream=prefix-kv-01 timeout=3.005s status=504
```

kevin_sre: Root cause hypothesis: cache cluster entered high-memory reclaim + persistence failures causing blocking RDB/AOF dumps, clients blocked, high latency -> our inference path blocks waiting on KV lookups for prefix caching and KV reads leading to whole request timeouts. Also seeing increased cache miss storms: elevated client-side cache miss during a hot-prefix sweep.

anya_support: Customer is on Hosted plan, heavy prompt prefix reuse. They rely on prefix cache for cold start token perf. They reported jump in token billing because retries triggered.

ryan_oncall: Short-term mitigations (immediately actionable):
- Disable prefix/KV cache reads for user-facing hosted inference routes (feature-flag on the gateway) so requests bypass Redis and fall back to local compute path. This will raise token cost but keep availability. @kevin_sre can we flip the flag?
- Increase client timeouts temporarily to 6s to reduce 502s while we heal Redis.
- Add a temporary rate-limit for ACME (or token-level soft-throttle) to reduce load.

kevin_sre: I can flip the gateway flag now: toggling `service.cache.prefix.enabled=false` on prod gateway. Starting rollback window: 09:18.

ops-bot: Applied config change to gateway-prod: service.cache.prefix.enabled=false by kevin_sre at 09:19:03Z

ryan_oncall: Confirming traffic: error rate for /v1/generate dropped from 23% -> 4% in the first 2 minutes after toggle. Latency improved for ACME. @anya_support please confirm with customer.

acme_infra: Confirmed. We see successful responses now, latency ~420ms typical, occasional 1s. Thanks for the quick fix. What's next?

kevin_sre: Next steps to restore durable cache: we're going to scale the Redis shard set from 3->5 nodes (add two read replicas and reconfigure memory limits), disable RDB snapshots temporarily to avoid blocking, and investigate AOF/RDB errors. I'll coordinate with infra to spin new instances.

kevin_sre: Commands I'm running (summarized):
```
# add nodes
terraform apply -var='redis_shard_count=5' -target=module.redis-prod
# set snapshotting off
redis-cli -h cache-prd-1 CONFIG SET save ""
# monitor
redis-cli -h cache-prd-1 INFO | egrep 'used_memory|evicted|blocked_clients'
```

ryan_oncall: Make sure to set `maxmemory-policy volatile-lru` for the prefix namespace and tune `maxmemory` per pod. Also add quick alert for 'blocked_clients > 10' so we can detect earlier.

kevin_sre: Understood. I'll also add a temporary per-prefix rate limiter for writes to reduce cache stampede.

support_jan: Customer-facing suggested message draft for ACME:
"We identified a Redis-backed cache service incident impacting some hosted inference requests. We have temporarily disabled the prefix cache for your requests to restore availability. Our engineering team is scaling and stabilizing the cache cluster; we'll follow up with a post-incident summary and action items. Apologies for the disruption. If you'd like us to revert cache behavior after recovery, we can coordinate a maintenance window."

anya_support: sending that now. Also open a billing note — customer saw extra retries and token consumption. Recommend issuing a usage credit for the spike window 09:05-09:20.

finance-bot: Created billing ticket BILL-20260315-09 for potential credit. Assigned to finance/ops.

kevin_sre: Redis scale and config changes applied. Monitoring shows blocked_clients dropping to 0 and used_memory normalized. Next: enable snapshotting once memory pressure is relieved and run a controlled cache warm-up (warm keys via low-rate bulk priming).

ryan_oncall: Plan for postmortem: (1) root cause analysis of persistence failure (RDB child exit), (2) add autoscale policy for Redis shard count, (3) improve cache fallback so prefix cache read failures degrade per-request rather than block on entire request, (4) add better observability (per-prefix miss rates, blocked_client alerts). I'll own the postmortem. Target ETA: preliminary within 48h.

deploy-bot: Incident #INC-20260315-17 updated: mitigated at 09:21 UTC. Next update requested in 2 hours.

anya_support: ACME acknowledged the note and accepted credits. Marking this thread resolved for support side; keeping incident open for engineering follow-up.

kevin_sre: leaving final note: avoid immediate aggressive cache rehydration — that'll spike load again. We'll do gradual ramp and watch 95/99 pct latency. Also recommend adding a read-through local in-process LRU for very hot prefixes to reduce blast radius.

ryan_oncall: thanks everyone. I'll file the postmortem and link here. Good job triaging quickly. :thumbsup:
